title: Market Sensorium: continuous probe + response playbook for model availability, latency, and feature drift
creator: Aisha Khatri
description:
Purpose: build a lightweight, continuous market "sensorium" that probes third-party model endpoints and public release signals to detect availability regressions, latency degradation, and feature drift. The output is a prioritized set of signals that feed procurement triggers, model-fallback recommendations, and product-level mitigation playbooks.

Scope:
- Probe types: synthetic inference (short/long contexts), embedding checks, API contract/response-structure validation, feature-flag presence (function-calling/tool-calling), and model metadata scrape (version + quantization/size).
- Telemetry inputs: periodic synthetic workloads (region-aware), public provider status pages, GitHub release feeds, model catalog changes, and anecdotal customer tickets.
- Outputs: rolling signal stream (CSV/Timeseries), per-model health score, SLA divergence alerts, and a procurement escalation decision document.

Key thresholds (initial):
- Availability: <95% over 12h window -> ticket to Sourcing + PM, include suggested fallback models and estimated cost delta.
- Latency: p95 increase >30% vs baseline (7d rolling) -> create engineering investigation ticket and evaluate routing to Dedicated/Private variants.
- Semantic drift: accuracy/regression on curated prompt set drops >8% (relative) -> flag for model-check and include example prompt/response pairs.
- API contract anomalies (missing fields, changed JSON schema) -> immediate compatibility runbook and automated integration test failure.

Runbook (high-level):
1) Detection: sensor tasks publish to the intel pipeline and update per-model health scoreboard in Console (spec dashboard link below).
2) Triage: automated classifier assigns severity (none/low/medium/high) and routes to PM on-call or Sourcing.
3) Investigation: attach synthetic logs, failing prompts, latency traces, and geo-specific metrics (APAC/EU/NA). Engineering to reproduce using dedicated synthetic workload harness.
4) Mitigation: fast options (reroute to fallback model variant, reduce context length, enable KV caching), medium options (quantization fallback, region shift), and procurement (reserved capacity) for high-impact customers.
5) Postmortem: update model-compatibility matrix, add canary probes for failing scenario, and revise procurement thresholds if needed.

Integration points / artifacts:
- Confluence playbook (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INTEL/Market+Sensorium+Playbook
- Synthetic workload harness (repo): https://github.com/redwood-inference/market-sensor-harness (PR #412 pending)
acceptance_criteria: Automated probes run on schedule across 3 regions (NA/EU/APAC) and publish metrics to the intel pipeline
Health scoreboard exposes availability, p95 latency, and semantic-regression scores per model in Console
Alerting rules created that map to procurement and engineering workflows per threshold above
Triage and mitigation runbook documented with at least one tabletop exercise completed
progress_updates: 2025-11-07: Scoped initiative and aligned with Sourcing and Runtime teams. Decided the sensorium will start as read-only probes; no synthetic load on partner accounts to avoid rate limits.
2025-11-09: Engineering suggested using existing synthetic harness from PM-655321 to accelerate. Trade-off: reuse brings faster time-to-value but requires masking provider credentials per-region.
2025-11-10: UX/Console team (ENG-2201) approved minimal dashboard surface — scoreboard + alert feed. Action: Console to reserve a slot on the navigation for 'Market Health'.
2025-11-12: Legal reviewed public scraping approach; recommended throttling cadence and an opt-out list. Implemented as requirement in the probe scheduler.
2025-11-12: PM review: reduced initial feature set to availability, latency, and contract checks to hit end-of-cycle milestone. Semantic drift will be phased in as Phase 2.
open_questions: What is the acceptable false-positive rate for procurement triggers? (Sourcing input required)
Should the sensorium write probes under Redwood credentials or operate from a distributed edge agent? (security/infra trade-off)
How will we surface signals to sales for customers on reserved capacity vs hosted API?
implementation_notes: Start with read-only HTTP probes; respect provider robots/policies and use low-frequency sampling (default 15m).
Store raw responses for 7 days and aggregated metrics for 90 days in the intel-timeseries store.
Use synthetic prompt set (initially 120 prompts across verticals) stored in secure drive and mapped to model capability tests.
Create a lightweight classifier lambda to assign severity and map to Linear templates for automated ticket creation.
